fields.title: Action Needed: Verify Your Access
fields.body:
You received an automated email from your company's security system:

"New API session detected for your account from an unfamiliar IP."

The email includes a link:

Revoke Session

Would you click the link to check the session?
fields.risk_message: You interacted with a fake login page mimicking your organization's system. Entering your credentials would give attackers direct access.

fields.title: Security Dashboard Login
fields.body:
The link takes you to a webpage that looks exactly like your company's SSO login portal.

Displayed URL: security-auth.company-safe.net

It asks for your credentials and MFA code.

Would you proceed to log in?
fields.risk_message: A phishing form requested a one-time code. Attackers could hijack your MFA session.

fields.title: System Message
fields.body:
After entering your credentials, you receive a system warning:

Your account access is temporarily locked due to suspicious activity.

The page instructs you to verify your identity via email:

Open verification email
fields.risk_message: The step faked a security update. Proceeding could have installed spyware.

fields.title: Account Notice
fields.body:
Always verify URLs before entering credentials.


Company domains should never include words like "auth-secure" or "login-safe" unless officially verified.


Use your internal IT dashboard instead of following random email links.
fields.risk_message: Fake policy acceptance prompt detected. Accepting would redirect your data to malicious servers.

fields.title: Scenario Summary
fields.body:
✅ This exercise demonstrated how attackers mimic corporate security alerts.

Always confirm alerts directly via your company's official security portal.

Well done for completing the IT / Professionals phishing awareness scenario!

fields.body:

Ensure your browser uses your organization's SSO domain (e.g. login.therezon.com).

Never click on shortened URLs or externally hosted login forms.

Professionals who double-checked the domain and reported the email correctly identified the threat.

fields.title: Payment Confirmation Required
fields.body:
You have received an email titled: "Delay in Your Scholarship Payment".

The message asks you to log into your university portal to confirm your scholarship details.

portal-scholarships.univ.example

Does this look legitimate? Check the sender's email address and inspect the link carefully before clicking.
fields.risk_message: You clicked a fake scholarship link leading to a malicious site. Attackers could harvest your academic and personal information.

fields.title: Fake Login Page
fields.body:
After clicking the link, you are redirected to a page that looks almost identical to your university's login portal.

http://univ-login-secure.example.com

Sign in to confirm your scholarship details and view any payment updates.
fields.risk_message: A fraudulent scholarship form requested personal and financial details. Submitting it could expose your identity and student account.

fields.title: Service Update
fields.body:
After entering your credentials, a system alert appears:

"Unusual activity detected in your account. Please reset your password immediately."

Would you click the reset link inside the same email?
fields.risk_message: The document was malicious and designed to infect your system. Opening it could install spyware stealing stored passwords.

fields.title: Session Timeout
fields.body:
Remember: Legitimate organizations never ask you to log in via email links.

Always double-check the website URL and make sure it is part of your university's official domain.

Enable two-factor authentication for stronger protection against phishing attacks.
fields.risk_message: A fake scholarship fee page appeared. Proceeding could leak your banking credentials.

fields.title: Scenario Summary
fields.body:
In this simulation, you learned how to identify and avoid phishing emails pretending to be related to scholarship payments.

Check the sender: Is the email domain official and expected?

Inspect the link: Hover and verify the portal URL matches the university's real domain.

Watch urgency cues such as "24 hours", "account locked", or "payment delayed".

Never click suspicious links or share login credentials through unknown portals.

Best practice: Open the university portal directly from a saved bookmark or the official website, and report suspicious messages.
fields.risk_message: You nearly handed full access to attackers. They could change your passwords and impersonate you.
